output.summary: Mandate 2038 is a 3–5 player strategy game lasting four Eras. In the Default Game, players use institutional Actions to build capability and authority; the faction with the most Mandate wins, while the shared World Ending is resolved separately. Advanced Play is excluded here.
keyRules: Setup uses a thirteen-tile board: Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational-ring tiles, and six shuffled public-ring tiles in evenly spaced outer positions.
Separate Headline cards by Era, use three Headlines per Era, and build a twelve-card Future Timeline. In Default Game, exclude cards marked Advanced Play.
Shuffle the Training deck. Divide twelve Era Mandate cards into four shuffled three-card Era decks.

Place shared tracks and components within reach, including Runway, Compute, Safety, Scrutiny, Systemic Risk, Joint Venture, Mega-Cluster, Initiative, and the Audit bag; place Power Source references nearby.
Each player receives their faction board, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, Generator, markers, Declare AGI card, and starting resources.
Place every CEO and one Team at Frontier; keep each faction’s other two Teams in supply. Set Runway, Compute, Capability, Customers, Trust, and Safety to printed starting values.
Place each faction’s printed public Mandate on the shared track. Put each player’s ten Scrutiny cubes outside the empty Audit bag.
Record the sum of printed starting Trust as Setup Collective Trust on the Era reference; this fixed value is used during the World Ending.

output.summary: The map uses 13 tiles in a sixfold-symmetric layout centered on Frontier. Six operational districts form an inner ring and six public districts form an outer ring; both rings are shuffled only within fixed tile pools. Movement is edge-based, up to two steps, and all setup pieces begin at Frontier. Non-Frontier hexes provide visit bonuses, two Facility spaces, production, and control values. Presence determines control, with ties controlled by nobody. District effects govern Training, Compute, deployment, building, funding, recruiting, Influence, Audit, Trust, Scrutiny, Power, and Frontier movement.
keyRules: Use exactly thirteen tiles: one Frontier, two Research Commons, two Compute Estates, and one each of Human Access District, Fabrication Corridor, Allocation Exchange, Workforce Transition District, Consensus Network, Civic Permission Authority, Power Corridor, and Thermal and Water Basin.

Place Frontier at the center. The six operational districts form a cycle around it; each touches Frontier, its two operational neighbors, and two adjoining public districts. Each public district touches exactly two operational districts and no other public district.
Shuffle the operational ring only among: one Research Commons, one Compute Estate, Fabrication Corridor, Allocation Exchange, Workforce Transition District, and Power Corridor.
Shuffle the public ring only among: one Research Commons, one Compute Estate, Human Access District, Consensus Network, Civic Permission Authority, and Thermal and Water Basin.

The inner and outer Research Commons are mechanically identical. The inner and outer Compute Estates are mechanically identical. Their visit effects, production, Facility spaces, and contract icons must match despite differing names, art, or flavor.
One movement step crosses one shared tile edge; a player may move up to two steps. Any tile is reachable from Frontier in two movement steps, while opposing outer tiles are four hexes apart.

All pieces placed during setup begin at Frontier. Frontier is a standing civic exception and cannot be controlled; once pieces leave it, positioning, Teams, local Power, and negotiated adjacency matter.
Presence values are CEO two, Team one, and Facility one. The player with the most presence controls a hex; tied presence means nobody controls it.
Every non-Frontier hex has a visit bonus, two Facility spaces, Facility production, and a control value used by Headlines and Mandates. Frontier has no Facility spaces.
Research Commons: once per Training Run, protect one duplicate as if spending Safety; each Facility produces one Safety; contract icon Compute.
Compute Estate: reduce the first Compute cost by one; each Facility produces two Compute; contract icon Compute.

Human Access District: deployment costs zero Compute; each Facility produces one Runway; contract icon Runway. Fabrication Corridor: building costs one less Runway; each Facility produces one Compute and one Runway; contract icon Compute. Allocation Exchange: Funding gains one Runway; each Facility produces two Runway; contract icon Runway. Workforce Transition District: recruiting costs one less Runway; each Facility may move one Team one hex during Production; contract icon Runway. Consensus Network: Influence may remove one additional Scrutiny; each Facility removes one Scrutiny before Audit; contract icon Runway. Civic Permission Authority: Influence may gain one additional Trust; each Facility produces one Trust; contract icon Runway. Power Corridor: an Emergency Power Complex may be built there for one Runway; each Facility produces one Compute; contract icon Compute. Thermal and Water Basin: a Civic Heat Battery may be built there for two Runway; each Facility removes one Scrutiny before Audit; contract icon Runway. Frontier: after Act, an acting player who ended movement there may gain one Runway and add one Scrutiny; Frontier has no production or Mandate and this optional effect does not modify the Action or create production or a Mandate.

keyRules: Progress: ready all Core Actions; 0 Escalation availability; 3 action cycles; Audit base 2. Unlocks Select → Move → Act, Training, starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Industrial Power, agreements, Civic Permission Authority votes, and Escalations are inactive.

Capacity: ready all Core Actions; gain 1 Escalation availability; 3 action cycles; Audit base 3. Default Game unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization. Advanced Play additionally unlocks two Links and the Network production bonus.

Authority: ready all Core Actions; gain 1 Escalation availability; 3 action cycles; Audit base 4. Unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Advanced Play additionally adds Civic Permission Authority votes and persistent Headline effects. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.

Continuity: ready all Core Actions; gain 2 Escalation availability; 3 action cycles; Audit base 5. Unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.

Dovetalis Labs starts with 5 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Deal Flow gains 1 Runway once per Era after an immediate trade giving at least 1 resource and receiving a different resource type. Shared Capacity Compact permits Joint Ventures with a player within 2 hexes; they remain active while both fixed host Facilities are powered and within 2 hexes.

Loopfold AI starts with 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 public Mandate. Its platform begins at 1 Customer and its next Deploy requires 4 Capability. The first Deploy each Era on a Human Access District or Consensus Network costs no Compute. Once per Era during Deploy, it may select any controlled Human Access District or Consensus Network as the destination remotely, receiving that tile's normal visit bonus and destination-dependent effects.

Mirevanta Works scores 1 Mandate at Capability 9 and 12, except in a five-player game where Capability 12 scores 2 Mandate. Controlled Negative Result triggers once per Era when a protectable duplicate would crash a Training Run: pay 1 Runway to discard it and immediately bank; it cannot protect the unprotectable Synthetic Loop duplicate. Substrate-Neutral Verification Standard is usable once per game during Research: each of the first 3 distinct domains banked grants 1 additional Capability; add 2 Scrutiny; no additional Action resolves.

output.summary: This chunk establishes the four Era cards, their cycle structure, audit bases, unlock timing, and all listed faction-board starting states and programs. It also confirms that Advanced Play additions are excluded from the default game.
keyRules: Each Era readies all Core Actions, plays 3 action cycles, and has an Era-specific Audit base: Progress 2, Capacity 3, Authority 4, Continuity 5.

Progress grants 0 Escalation availability and unlocks Select → Move → Act, Training, the starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Industrial Power, agreements, Civic Permission Authority votes, and Escalations are inactive.
Capacity grants 1 Escalation availability and unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization in the default game. Advanced Play-only unlocks are Links and the Network production bonus.

Authority grants 1 Escalation availability and unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Advanced Play-only additions are Civic Permission Authority votes and persistent Headline effects. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.
Continuity grants 2 Escalation availability and unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Earlier unused Escalations remain available.
Loopfold AI starts with 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 public Mandate.
Loopfold’s Platform sequence begins at 1 Customer; its next Deploy requires 4 Capability.
Loopfold’s Installed Base program makes the first Deploy each Era on a Human Access District or Consensus Network cost 0 Compute.

Loopfold’s Social Graph program can be used once per Era during Deploy to choose any controlled Human Access District or Consensus Network as the destination without moving there; that remote tile provides its normal visit bonus and all destination-dependent Deploy effects.

Dovetalis starts with 5 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Deal Flow grants 1 Runway once per Era after an immediate trade giving at least 1 resource and receiving a different resource type.
Dovetalis’s Shared Capacity Compact allows Joint Ventures with a player within 2 hexes; they remain active while both fixed host Facilities are powered and within 2 hexes.

Mirevanta starts with 3 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Its Peer Validation scores Capability 9 and 12 for Mandate, except Capability 12 scores 2 Mandate in a five-player game. Scientific Method can once per Era protect a protectable duplicate from a Training Run crash by paying 1 Runway, discarding it, and immediately banking; it cannot protect Synthetic Loop’s unprotectable duplicate. Scaling-Law Breakthrough is once per game during Research, adds 1 Capability for each of the first 3 distinct domains banked, adds 2 Scrutiny, and resolves no additional Action; it is available in Continuity when signature faction programs unlock unless otherwise specified by setup timing above it being printed on board for later use. (Need verify exact timing.)

keyRules: Corthaven starts with 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 starting public Mandate.
The Shovels: when another player spends at least 2 Compute in one action, Corthaven gains 1 Runway, at most twice per Era.

Allocation Window: once during Capacity, after a Headline resolves and before Action selection, create 2 temporary Compute. For each token, make one complete rival offer at a Runway price no higher than that rival's current Runway. The rival may accept, reject, or make one lower counterprice; Corthaven may accept or reject it. No replacement offer or further counter is allowed. Temporary Compute disappears at cycle end, whether sold or unsold.
Fund: gain 2 Runway, or gain 4 Runway and add 2 Scrutiny.
Research: spend 1 Compute to conduct a push-your-luck Training Run.
Build: construct a Facility or Generator; Links are permitted only in Advanced Play.
Organize: recruit, redistribute Teams, or relocate a Facility.
Deploy: spend 1 Compute to gain a Customer if Capability permits.
Influence: use political presence to gain Trust, remove Scrutiny, or negotiate from a Facility.

Mega-Cluster: spend 3 Runway and 2 Compute to place one across an eligible Facility edge; joint funding uses the stated lead/partner payment and one acceptance decision. It demands 2 additional Power, produces 3 Compute, and adds 2 Scrutiny.
Reorganization: move every Team up to one hex; optionally return one Team for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny. It does not ready or resolve another Action.

Open Weights: everyone gains 1 Capability; Corthaven gains 2 Trust and removes 1 Scrutiny. Once per player per game after spending an Escalation availability, if unlocked and selected as applicable to the global rules context. output.summary: Mirevanta Works (seat 1, engine seat 0) is a capability-rushing imperial research lab in a four-Era, three-action-cycle-per-Era Default Game. Setup begins on a 13-tile board with all CEOs and one Team at Frontier, shuffled operational and public rings, four Era decks, a 12-card Future Timeline, shared tracks, Audit bag, and faction components. Mirevanta starts with Owen Okafor, 3 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Its key abilities are Mandate at Capability 9 and 12, Controlled Negative Result once per Era for a protectable Research duplicate, and Substrate-Neutral Verification Standard once per game during Research.
rulesReconstruction: Setup: place Frontier centrally, arrange the six operational tiles in the inner ring and six public tiles in the outer ring, shuffling only within their respective pools. Place all CEOs and one Team at Frontier. Set faction tracks and resources to printed values; give Mirevanta its four Facilities, Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, AGI card, Scrutiny cubes, Customer markers, and other faction components. Record the sum of printed starting Trust as Setup Collective Trust. Randomize Initiative and begin Era I.

Each Era has three action cycles per player. At the start of the Era, advance to its Era card, ready all six Core Actions, reveal one of the Era's three Mandate cards and return the other two unseen, and award the Era's Escalation availability. Era I has no Escalations; Era II adds one; Era III adds one while retaining unused availability; Era IV adds two.

Each action cycle: reveal a Headline into the current Era's Future Timeline row; players secretly select an unused Core Action or an available unlocked Escalation; reveal simultaneously; resolve clockwise from Initiative. The active player moves one CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent steps, then resolves the selected Action at the destination, applying any visit bonus. Pass Initiative clockwise.

The six Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny through Venture funding; Allocation Exchange adds one Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits, moves pieces, or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute and the next Customer's Capability threshold, unless Human Access District waives Compute; every Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence changes Trust/Scrutiny or creates or terminates an eligible Joint Venture.

Research uses push-your-luck Training. Ordinary domains are Code, Science, Web, Books, Images, Video, and Synthetic; the first card from each adds provisional Capability. The player may bank and stop after a non-duplicate. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, losing provisional Capability and adding 1 Scrutiny. Safety, a Research Commons visit, or Mirevanta's Controlled Negative Result can protect a protectable duplicate; protection discards it and immediately banks. Mirevanta's Substrate-Neutral Verification Standard can add 1 Capability for each of the first three distinct domains banked, adds 2 Scrutiny, and resolves no extra Action.

Mirevanta's faction Mandate is already public and is not scored again. It scores 1 Mandate on first reaching Capability 9 and 1 on first reaching Capability 12, except Capability 12 is worth 2 in a five-player game. Other permanent Mandate sources include Customer gains, first-time Capability thresholds at 3/6/9/12, Trust thresholds at 2/4/6, Headlines, Era Mandates, Fusion, AGI, and printed faction effects.

Era II unlocks Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization. A Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, adds 2 Scrutiny, uses matched tokens, and requires its acting piece to end on a host hex. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny; it does not ready or resolve another Action.

Era III unlocks Joint Ventures, immediate Power purchases, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability, with additional effects not fully recorded. Narrative Capture allows removing two personal Scrutiny, gaining 2 Runway, or giving a player with more Customers than you 1 Scrutiny.

Era IV unlocks Agent Swarms, Declare AGI, Fusion, and faction programs. Agent Swarm combines two different unused Core Actions, resolves both after one move, exhausts both, flips the Agent Swarm, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI is a global-after-movement effect requiring Capability 9+, three Customers, three Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and paying 5 Runway; it occupies a Fusion slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Production is synchronized globally after the action cycles according to the Era's procedure. Power is capacity, cannot be stored, and is assigned once among legal recipients. Facilities require complete demand and legal local Power to operate. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after successfully operating in completed Production; relocation, loss of legal Power, or insufficient Power flips it offline. Resource caps apply immediately after gains: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3 unless faction text overrides them.

Audit uses the Era base: 2 in Era I, 3 in Era II, 4 in Era III, and 5 in Era IV, with Scrutiny cubes entering the bag according to the applicable procedures. Scrutiny can be removed by returning that faction's cubes from the Audit bag to supply. Era IV colored cubes cost 2 Runway or 1 Mandate, while black cubes impose the current Era penalty on qualifying players; exact application still needs confirmation.

At End of Era, complete the Era's global Production, Audit, and any Era-specific effects in the authoritative order, then score the revealed Era Mandate if its minimum qualification is met. The qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Mandate comparison uses only the printed criterion on that Mandate. Keep the scored card face up beside its Era as public history. Then continue to the next Era, readying Core Actions and awarding the next Era's availability.

At game end, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud Era by Era. Subtract 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero. Determine the shared World Ending from final Trust, AGI declarations, and unresolved Systemic Risk in the Audit bag. AGI emerges if at least one declarer finishes at Capability 9 or higher. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is lower than player count. AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity. Read that narrative, then announce the highest-Mandate institution. Ties break by Trust, Customers, Compute, then joint victory. Facilities and control provide no additional endgame Mandate.

output.summary: Kestralyn (engine seat 1) begins the four-Era Default Game at Frontier with CEO Jiwon Park, one Team, 6 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. The game uses simultaneous Core Action selection, clockwise resolution, and Select → Move → Act turns. Highest final Mandate wins; the shared World Ending is resolved separately.
rulesReconstruction: Use Default Game only; exclude Advanced Play, Tactics, secret objectives, Links, persistent Advanced Headlines, and other ◆ procedures.

Build the thirteen-tile board: Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational tiles around it, and six shuffled public tiles outside. All setup CEOs and initial Teams begin at Frontier. Frontier has no Facility spaces and is not controllable property.

Use four Eras in Progress → Capacity → Authority → Continuity order. Each Era has three action cycles. At Era setup, ready all six Core Actions, grant the Era's Escalation availability, apply its unlocks, reveal three Era Headlines, and create the Era's three-card Mandate deck.
Record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of starting Trust values. Kestralyn contributes 2. This fixed value is used only for the final Open-ending comparison.

Each quarter begins by advancing the Era card, reading its New this Era strip, revealing one Mandate from the current Era deck and boxing the other two unseen, readying all Core Actions, and awarding Escalation availability.

Each action cycle reveals one Headline. Players secretly select one Core Action and reveal simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative: select, move, then act. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

The six Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives either 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway with 2 Scrutiny; Allocation Exchange adds 1 Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and begins a Training Run. Build constructs a Facility or, from Era II onward, an ordinary Generator. Organize recruits or moves pieces. Exact Deploy and Influence procedures remain dependent on the referenced rules.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete resource offer to one rival. One counteroffer is allowed. Accepted Runway, Compute, or Safety transfers occur immediately; promises are non-binding. Persistent ventures, lobbying, or Trust manipulation require the relevant action or printed window.

Movement crosses shared tile edges; CEOs and Teams move up to two steps. Presence is CEO 2, Team 1, Facility 1. Highest presence controls a non-Frontier hex; ties give control to nobody. Rival pieces coexist without combat or elimination.

Facilities require two Runway, occupy one of two spaces on a non-Frontier hex, and require one Power during Production. Kestralyn's first Facility Build each Era costs one less Runway; if that discount actually reduces the Runway paid for a completed Facility, Kestralyn gains 1 Mandate.

Kestralyn may use Orbital Compute once per game during movement to move one Facility instead of the acting piece to any legal open Facility space. Attached components and designations move with it; Power eligibility is recalculated, and if available capacity can power it, its printed production resolves immediately once. Add 2 Scrutiny.

Production uses local Power. The starting grid powers only its assigned first Facility. Each Generator powers Facilities on its own or an adjacent hex; Facilities cannot pass Power onward. Each Facility needs one Power, while a Mega-Cluster needs two additional Power. Offline Facilities produce nothing.

Customers produce 1 Runway each during Production. Customers 1–3 score 2 Mandate each; Customers 4–5 score 1 each. Resource caps are Runway 12, Compute 10, and Safety 3 unless faction rules modify them. Capability is permanent and spent only when instructed.

Research Training Runs reveal and resolve Training cards. The first card from each ordinary domain gives 1 provisional Capability; banking converts all provisional Capability to permanent Capability and ends the run. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, losing provisional Capability, adding 1 Scrutiny, ending the run, and discarding revealed cards. Safety or a Research Commons visit can protect one duplicate, but protection immediately banks and ends the run.

Era II unlocks Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization. Era III unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability; Kestralyn's faction-specific modification is not supplied. Narrative Capture occurs globally after movement and allows removing 2 Scrutiny, gaining 2 Runway, or giving 1 Scrutiny to a player with more Customers.

Era IV unlocks Kestralyn's signature programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Agent Swarm uses two different unused Core Actions, one movement, both actions from the destination in either order, one visit bonus, exhausts both actions, flips the Swarm state, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. Grid-Ready status must have been earned during completed Production with full legal Power. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5. Every declaration adds 3 Scrutiny. It does not itself end the game.

Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway. It uses the Fusion marker, occupies a Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny. It cannot be built if all three shared Generator slots are occupied or Power Corridor is full.

At End-of-Era Resolution, resolve the revealed Era Mandate according to its printed qualification. If nobody qualifies, no one scores. Otherwise the qualifying leader gains 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders gain 1 each. Scored Mandates remain public beside the Era.

Apply the Era's Production and other stated end-of-Era effects according to the authoritative Production, Headline, and Era procedures. Grid-Ready status is checked after Production; Facilities with complete demand and legal Power flip Grid-Ready, while relocated, disconnected, or underpowered Facilities flip back or remain offline. Unresolved action, Escalation, Headline, Audit, and Systemic Risk handling is not fully recorded in these notes.

Each Era has three simultaneous-selection action cycles, followed by Production and Mandate handling. Advanced Play, Tactics, and secret objectives are excluded.
rulesReconstruction: Setup: place Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. Place all setup pieces instructed by the faction and rules at Frontier; rival pieces coexist and Frontier cannot be controlled.

Separate each Era’s non-Advanced Headlines and Mandates. Use three Headlines per Era and three Mandates per Era; create the twelve-card Future Timeline. Shuffle the 50-card Training deck. Place shared resources, the Audit bag, Initiative marker, Power references, contract pairs, Mega-Cluster pairs, and Fusion marker.

Corthaven receives its board, CEO Eli Rosen, three Teams, four Facilities, Generator, starting-grid identifier, markers, Core Actions, Escalations, AGI card, and ten Scrutiny cubes. Its printed starting state is 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Its printed faction abilities include The Shovels and the Capacity-era Allocation Window.

Record Setup Collective Trust by summing all factions’ printed starting Trust. Keep each faction’s ten Scrutiny cubes outside the empty Audit bag. Choose Initiative randomly and begin the first Era, Progress.

At the start of each Era, read the Era card’s New this Era strip, ready all six Core Actions, reveal the Era’s Mandate card according to the Mandate rules, and award that Era’s Escalation availability. Progress grants 0; Capacity grants 1 and unlocks Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization; Authority grants 1 and unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture; Continuity grants 2 and unlocks Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion, and faction programs.

Each of the three cycles is: reveal one Headline into the current Future Timeline row; players secretly select one unused Core Action or an unlocked Escalation by spending one availability; reveal simultaneously; resolve clockwise from Initiative; then pass Initiative clockwise.

For each selected action, resolve Select → Move → Act. Move one CEO or Team 0–2 adjacent steps, then resolve the chosen Action from the destination. The destination determines applicable visit bonuses, action legality, Facility placement, Research, Deploy, Influence, and infrastructure effects. Exhaust used Core Actions or flip used Escalations after resolution.

A selected action cannot be replaced if blocked after reveal. Resolve any remaining legal mode, piece, movement, target, payment, or immediate trade permitted by the rules; the precise no-legal-resolution fallback remains unspecified in the notes.

Corthaven’s Fund offers 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway with 2 Scrutiny. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training. Build constructs a Facility or, from Capacity onward, a Generator. Organize recruits, redistributes Teams, or relocates a Facility for 1 Runway. Deploy costs 1 Compute and gains 1 Customer if the Capability threshold is met, adding 1 Scrutiny. Influence can change Trust, remove Scrutiny, or negotiate/create/terminate a Joint Venture.

In Capacity, Corthaven may use Allocation Window once per Era after a Headline resolves and before selection: create 2 temporary Compute and make one complete offer per token to rivals. Each rival may accept, reject, or make one lower counteroffer; Corthaven may accept or reject. Temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

Escalations are once per player per game. Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute solo, or joint funding of 2 Runway/1 Compute from the lead and 1 Runway/1 Compute from the partner; it requires additional Power, uses a matched token pair, produces 3 Compute, and adds 2 Scrutiny. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny. Open Weights grants every player 1 Capability. Narrative Capture removes 2 Scrutiny, gains 2 Runway, or gives 1 Scrutiny to a player with more Customers. Agent Swarm uses two different unused Core Actions, resolves both from one destination, exhausts both, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Declare AGI is available in Continuity and requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5; each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway; it occupies a Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

At Production, process every player through each box before advancing: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner. Generators generate capacity and Emergency Power Complexes add Scrutiny. Players may request one Power purchase from one adjacent rival; accepted purchases cost 1 Runway per Power and last only this Production. Allocate starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency Power to legal Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Produce powered Facilities, Customer income, active Mega-Clusters, and then resolve active Joint Ventures in contract-number order.

Each Customer produces 1 Runway during Production. Customers 1–3 immediately score 2 public Mandate; Customers 4–5 score 1. Capability thresholds 3, 6, 9, and 12 normally score 2 Mandate, subject to Corthaven-independent faction modifications. Trust thresholds 2, 4, and 6 each score 2 Mandate. Resource caps are Runway 12, Compute 10, and Safety 3.

After Production, flip Facilities Grid-Ready only if they received complete demand. Relocation, loss of legal Power eligibility, or insufficient Production Power flips them back. Offline Facilities retain occupancy and presence but produce nothing. Risk Scrutiny enters the Audit bag; Audit draws use the Era/player-count table and impose Runway, Trust, or Mandate penalties. Black Systemic Risk cubes impose the current Era’s penalty on players with at least 3 Customers.

Score the revealed Era Mandate immediately: qualification is determined only by its printed criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Keep the scored card publicly beside its Era. Then proceed to the next Era and repeat the three-cycle and Production sequence.

At game end, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud Era by Era. Each player loses 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero. Determine AGI emergence, final Collective Trust, and unresolved black Systemic Risk in the Audit bag.

The ending is Open if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is lower than player count. Each Era has three action cycles per player. At the start of the Era, advance to its Era card, ready all six Core Actions, reveal one of the Era's three Mandate cards and return the other two unseen, and award the Era's Escalation availability. Era I has no Escalations; Era II adds one; Era III adds one while retaining unused availability; Era IV adds two.

Each action cycle: reveal a Headline into the current Era's Future Timeline row; players secretly select an unused Core Action or an available unlocked Escalation; reveal simultaneously; resolve clockwise from Initiative. The active player moves one CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent steps, then resolves the selected Action at the destination, applying any visit bonus. Pass Initiative clockwise.

The six Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny through Venture funding; Allocation Exchange adds one Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits, moves pieces, or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute and the next Customer's Capability threshold, unless Human Access District waives Compute; every Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence changes Trust/Scrutiny or creates or terminates an eligible Joint Venture.

Research uses push-your-luck Training. Ordinary domains are Code, Science, Web, Books, Images, Video, and Synthetic; the first card from each adds provisional Capability. The player may bank and stop after a non-duplicate. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, losing provisional Capability and adding 1 Scrutiny. Safety, a Research Commons visit, or Mirevanta's Controlled Negative Result can protect a protectable duplicate; protection discards it and immediately banks. Mirevanta's Substrate-Neutral Verification Standard can add 1 Capability for each of the first three distinct domains banked, adds 2 Scrutiny, and resolves no extra Action.

Mirevanta's faction Mandate is already public and is not scored again. It scores 1 Mandate on first reaching Capability 9 and 1 on first reaching Capability 12, except Capability 12 is worth 2 in a five-player game. Other permanent Mandate sources include Customer gains, first-time Capability thresholds at 3/6/9/12, Trust thresholds at 2/4/6, Headlines, Era Mandates, Fusion, AGI, and printed faction effects.

Era II unlocks Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization. A Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, adds 2 Scrutiny, uses matched tokens, and requires its acting piece to end on a host hex. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny; it does not ready or resolve another Action.

Era III unlocks Joint Ventures, immediate Power purchases, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability, with additional effects not fully recorded. Narrative Capture allows removing two personal Scrutiny, gaining 2 Runway, or giving a player with more Customers than you 1 Scrutiny.

Era IV unlocks Agent Swarms, Declare AGI, Fusion, and faction programs. Agent Swarm combines two different unused Core Actions, resolves both after one move, exhausts both, flips the Agent Swarm, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI is a global-after-movement effect requiring Capability 9+, three Customers, three Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Production is synchronized globally after the action cycles according to the Era's procedure. Power is capacity, cannot be stored, and is assigned once among legal recipients. Facilities require complete demand and legal local Power to operate. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after successfully operating in completed Production; relocation, loss of legal Power, or insufficient Power flips it offline. Capability thresholds 3, 6, 9, and 12 normally score 2 Mandate, subject to Corthaven-independent faction modifications. Trust thresholds 2, 4, and 6 each score 2 Mandate. Resource caps are Runway 12, Compute 10, and Safety 3.

After Production, flip Facilities Grid-Ready only if they received complete demand. Relocation, loss of legal Power eligibility, or insufficient Production Power flips them back. Offline Facilities retain occupancy and presence but produce nothing. Risk Scrutiny enters the Audit bag; Audit draws use the Era/player-count table and impose Runway, Trust, or Mandate penalties. Black Systemic Risk cubes impose the current Era’s penalty on players with at least 3 Customers.

Score the revealed Era Mandate immediately: qualification is determined only by its printed criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Keep the scored card publicly beside its Era. Then proceed to the next Era and repeat the three-cycle and Production sequence.

At game end, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud Era by Era. Each player loses 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero. Determine AGI emergence, final Collective Trust, and unresolved black Systemic Risk in the Audit bag.

The ending is Open if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is lower than player count. If AGI emerges, Open yields The Singularity and Closed yields The Closed Loop. Without AGI, Open yields The Plural Future and Closed yields Assured Continuity. Read the corresponding World Ending narrative. Only afterward announce the institution with the highest Mandate; Facilities, control, stored resources, and unused cards provide no separate final Mandate.

output.summary: Default Game is a four-Era, public-information game. Loopfold AI begins with 4 Runway, 2 Compute, 0 Capability, 1 Customer, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 4 Mandate. The institution with the most final Mandate wins; the World Ending is evaluated separately.
rulesReconstruction: Use Default Game only; exclude Advanced Play, Tactics, and secret objectives.

Build the fixed thirteen-tile board: Frontier in the center, six operational districts in the inner ring, and six public districts in the outer ring. Shuffle only within each ring. Place all setup pieces at Frontier; Frontier cannot be controlled and has no Facility spaces.

Shuffle eligible Era Headline cards and Era Mandate cards separately. Each Era ultimately uses three Headlines and reveals one Mandate from its three-card Era deck; resolved Headlines form the twelve-card Future Timeline.

Set shared tracks, the empty Audit bag, Power references, Initiative, and component supplies. Each faction receives its board, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, Generator, Core Actions, Escalations, AGI card, markers, and starting resources. Loopfold’s starting-grid Facility and face remain unspecified.
Begin Era I with randomly selected Initiative. Each Era has three action cycles.

At the start of each cycle, reveal one Headline into that Era’s Future Timeline row. Resolve any required pre-selection effects, then players secretly select and simultaneously reveal one Core Action.

Resolve players clockwise from Initiative. Each player selects movement of 0–2 steps, then resolves the selected Action at the destination. A consumed target can cause a later committed Action to move and exhaust without effect or compensation.

The six Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives either 2 Runway or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny; Research costs 1 Compute and runs Training; Build constructs a Facility or Generator; Organize recruits, redistributes Teams, or relocates a Facility; Deploy advances Customers when Capability permits; Influence handles Trust, Scrutiny, lobbying, ventures, and related negotiations.

A player may make one complete offer to one rival immediately before or after Act. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be exchanged. The recipient may accept, reject, or issue one complete counteroffer. Promises are non-binding.

Initiative passes clockwise after each action-resolution cycle. Era unlocks are Progress, Capacity, Authority, and Continuity. They activate Training, Facilities, Customers, Scrutiny, Generators, Mega-Clusters, agreements, Open Weights, Narrative Capture, signature programs, Agent Swarm, AGI, and Fusion at their respective Eras.

At the start of each Era, read the next Era card, apply its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability. Unused Escalations remain available where specified.

Resolve Production synchronously by box: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner, then Audit. Generators operate automatically when they have eligible local Facilities; Power is allocated only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Powered Facilities, Customers, Mega-Clusters, and Joint Ventures produce according to their printed rules.

At the end of Production, update Grid-Ready status. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after receiving complete demand during completed Production; relocation, loss of legal Power eligibility, or insufficient Production Power flips it offline.

Resolve Audit using the Era/player-count draw count. Colored cubes penalize their owners; Era IV costs are two Runway or one Mandate. Black Systemic Risk cubes apply the current Era penalty. Drawn colored cubes return to supply; undrawn cubes remain in the bag.

End-of-Era Mandate scoring uses the revealed card’s printed criterion only. If nobody qualifies, score nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, or tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Keep scored Mandates beside the Era as public history.

Mandate is also awarded immediately for Customers, first-time Capability thresholds of 3/6/9/12, first-time Trust thresholds of 2/4/6, Headlines, Fusion, faction effects, and AGI. Threshold awards are permanent; holdings and unused resources do not score unless explicitly instructed.

After Era IV, read all twelve Headlines aloud by Era, lose 1 Mandate for each offline Facility, then resolve the World Ending. Count AGI declarations, final Collective Trust, and unresolved black Systemic Risk cubes.

AGI emerges if at least one declaring institution finishes with Capability at least 9. The ending is Open if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is lower than player count. AGI/Open is The Singularity; AGI/Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI/Open is The Plural Future; no AGI/Closed is Assured Continuity.

The highest-Mandate institution wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then joint victory with the stated merger announcement. Facilities, controlled hexes, stored resources, and other holdings provide no separate endgame Mandate.

answers.answer: The session is provisionally a four-player session.

At Era start: advance to the next fixed Era card, read its “New this Era” strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award Escalation availability. Each Era then has three action cycles, followed by Power and Production, Public Audit, and Mandate scoring. Era-specific unlocks activate at Era start; the complete Mandate-scoring procedure is: if nobody qualifies, nobody scores; otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, with tied qualifying leaders scoring 1 each. The scored card remains public beside its Era.

If a committed Action becomes blocked, movement still resolves and the Action exhausts without effect or compensation. The Action cannot be replaced or rewound; rejected, passed, or unanswered immediate trade requests likewise leave it blocked.

citations.heading: A committed Action that becomes blocked

answers.answer: Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability; the acting player gains 2 Trust and removes 1 Scrutiny. Era III unlocks immediate Power purchases, but the packets do not provide the complete purchase rules.

Production is synchronized as Generate, Power Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Generators operate automatically when locally eligible. Power is assigned only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters; each Facility needs 1 Power and each Mega-Cluster needs 2 additional Power. Fully powered Facilities become Grid-Ready; insufficient Power removes that status. Purchased Power lasts only for that Production, and suppliers may sell at most one Power. Powered Facilities, Customers, and active Mega-Clusters produce; active Joint Ventures are partnered by contract number. Audit draws the Era/player-count profile, resolves colored cubes as Runway-or-Trust losses in Eras I–III and two Runway-or-one Mandate losses in Era IV, and applies black-cube penalties. Power Corridor supports an Emergency Power Complex of 4 Power with +1 Scrutiny each Production; Thermal or Water Basin supports a Civic Heat Battery of 3 Power with +1 Trust on construction and no recurring penalty.

The center is Frontier. The six operational-ring tiles are Research Commons, Compute Estate, Fabrication Corridor, Allocation Exchange, Workforce Transition District, and Power Corridor. The six public-ring tiles are Research Commons, Compute Estate, Human Access District, Consensus Network, Civic Permission Authority, and Thermal and Water Basin. Both rings are shuffled. Mirevanta’s integrated starting-grid identifier is not specified.

Era IV draws 3, 4, 5, 6, or 8 Audit cubes for 2–6 players. Each colored cube costs 2 Runway or 1 Mandate; with fewer than 2 Runway, lose 1 Mandate if possible, otherwise reduce Runway to zero. Mandate cannot fall below zero. A black cube gives every player with at least 3 Customers the current Era’s penalty, but the packet does not specify the exact current-Era black-cube penalty or all player-count rounding rules.

The packets do not identify which specific Headlines, Era Mandates, and faction programs are selected for this session, nor provide every complete card text. They establish that printed cards are authoritative; the cited records identify faction, Escalation, several Headline, and Mandate texts.

The thirteen tiles and ring pools are specified, but their shuffled physical arrangement is not. Adjacency is sixfold-symmetric: each operational district touches Frontier, its two operational neighbors, and two adjoining public districts; each public district touches exactly two operational districts and no public district.

Setup places every CEO and one Team at Frontier, with two Teams per faction in supply. Each faction uses its printed starting values; printed public Mandates are placed on the shared track. Ten Scrutiny cubes per player begin outside an empty Audit bag, and Initiative is chosen randomly. The packets do not give the chosen Initiative player or the complete physical setup requested.

Deploy costs 1 Compute for 1 Customer, except Human Access District waives the Compute cost; every Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence moves normally, then at specified public districts grants Trust or removes Scrutiny, or at a Facility creates a Joint Venture with an eligible rival Facility. Joint Ventures require explicit consent; rejection, pass, or no response consumes the effect. The packets do not provide the complete Default Game destination, agreement, and control procedures.

The synchronized sequence is Generate, Power Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Generators operate automatically when locally eligible. Starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency Power may go only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters; each Facility requires 1 Power, each Mega-Cluster 2 additional Power, and complete demand makes a Facility Grid-Ready while insufficient Power removes that status. Purchased Power lasts only for that Production; offline Facilities produce nothing and may recover when later sufficiently powered. Joint Ventures require both hosts powered.

A Headline is revealed at the beginning of each cycle, before secret action selection, placed in the current Era’s Future Timeline row, and resolved by its printed effect and duration. It normally expires at cycle end unless it names that Era’s Production; resolved cards remain face up. Narrative Capture is global after movement. Immediate resource trades occur immediately before or after Act. The packets do not fully specify all Headline cleanup or Narrative Capture timing interactions.

Escalations are selected by spending 1 Escalation availability and are once per player per game. Era II grants 1 availability and unlocks Mega-Cluster and Reorganization; Era III grants 1 additional availability and unlocks Open Weights and Narrative Capture; Era IV grants 2 and unlocks Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Previously unlocked unused Escalations remain available; unspent availability expires at Era end. Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, demands 2 additional Power, produces 3 Compute, and adds 2 Scrutiny. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway plus 1 Scrutiny. Agent Swarm resolves two different unused Core Actions from one destination, exhausts both, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion on Power Corridor spends 5 Runway to construct 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny. The packets do not fully define all refresh and carry-forward interfaces.

The exact revealed Era Mandate card is not identified. The revealed card controls qualification and scoring: if nobody meets its minimum qualification, nobody scores; otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate, with tied qualifying leaders scoring 1 each. Examples of stated minimums include 2 total Power demand, 1 Joint Venture, and 4 Trust.

The packets establish that Production is followed by Public Audit and Mandate scoring; the scored Mandate remains public history. Setup Collective Trust is the sum of printed starting Trust values and is fixed for the World Ending. Final scoring loses 1 Mandate per offline Facility, but the packets do not define the complete End-of-Era cleanup, retained-system, or offline-identification procedure.
The packets do not specify which Corthaven Facility face is up, how the integrated starting-grid identifier is matched to the first Facility, or the resulting initial placement.

The packets specify the thirteen-tile ring pools and sixfold adjacency, plus one-step-per-shared-edge movement, up to two movement steps, control values, two Facility spaces on every non-Frontier hex, visit bonuses, and district production. They do not specify the post-shuffle physical layout requested.

A committed Action cannot be replaced. If a required target is consumed or no legal resolution remains, movement still resolves and the Action exhausts without effect or compensation. The packets do not separately resolve every listed failure mode, such as no legal piece, mode, payment, or immediate trade.

answers.answer: Corthaven’s Allocation Window creates 2 temporary Compute. For each token, Corthaven makes one complete offer to a rival at a Runway price no greater than that rival’s current Runway. The rival may accept, reject, or make one lower counterprice, which Corthaven may accept or reject. No replacement offer or further counter is allowed; temporary Compute disappears at cycle end. The packets do not state whether these tokens may be used for anything besides the required offers.

For a joint Mega-Cluster, the lead names the partner and both host Facilities. The lead pays 2 Runway and 1 Compute; the partner pays 1 Runway and 1 Compute. The packets do not specify how the lead is represented or whether leadership can change.

Starting-grid capacity powers only its assigned first Facility. Generators may power Facilities on their own or adjacent hexes; assign each source only among legal local recipients. Purchased and emergency Power are also limited to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters. The packets provide no complete priority rule for competing eligible recipients.

The sequence is: begin the quarter and reveal the Era Mandate; resolve three action cycles; complete synchronized Power and Production; conduct Public Audit; then score the Mandate. Escalation availability is awarded when the Era begins. The packets do not provide a complete End-of-Era procedure beyond this sequence.
Final ties are broken by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute. If still tied, the institutions share victory with an extremely serious merger announcement.

The Headline contract is three non-Advanced cards revealed per Era, with resolved cards face up in that Era’s row, forming a twelve-card Future Timeline. Headlines are revealed before secret action selection and normally expire at cycle end unless they name that Era’s Production. Exact physical card identities and Era Mandate timing/text are not provided.
The packets do not identify Loopfold’s integrated starting-grid Facility, its starting face, or its initial placement.

Era unlocks become active at the beginning of that Era when its fixed Era card is advanced to and its “New this Era” strip is read. Progress unlocks Select → Move → Act, Training, starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny; Capacity unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, and Reorganization; Authority unlocks agreements, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture; Continuity unlocks signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator. Escalation availability is 0, 1, 1, and 2 respectively; earlier unused Escalations are retained from Authority onward.

The Audit bag starts empty, with ten Scrutiny cubes per player outside it. The exact black Systemic Risk penalty in each Era is not provided. In Era IV, a black cube gives every player with at least 3 Customers the current Era’s penalty; black cubes remaining at game end are unresolved Systemic Risk.

Power and Production proceed as Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Generators operate automatically if they have at least one locally eligible Facility. Each Facility requires 1 delivered Power; a Mega-Cluster requires 2 additional Power. Starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency Power may be assigned only to legal local Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Complete demand grants Grid-Ready; insufficient Power removes it. Purchased Power lasts only for the current Production. Emergency Power Complex provides 4 Power and adds 1 Scrutiny each Production; Civic Heat Battery provides 3 permanent Power with no recurring penalty.

Build has Facility and Infrastructure modes. Constructing a Facility costs 2 Runway and places it on the acting piece’s hex; constructing a Generator requires an acting piece on an Energy hex. Deploy spends Compute for a Customer and adds Scrutiny. Influence moves normally, then resolves a legal district or Joint Venture effect. Movement is up to two steps across shared edges. The packets do not provide complete procedures for every Core Action, destination bonus, or blocked-target timing.

Setup Collective Trust is the sum of every faction’s printed starting Trust and is recorded as a fixed value on the Era reference for the World Ending. Final scoring loses 1 Mandate per offline Facility, with Mandate unable to fall below zero. The packets do not define the operational procedure for identifying final offline Facilities.
